newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli economic activity stabilises, data show.
newsitem.headline: Israeli economic activity stabilises, data show.

text.p: Indicators for the last two months of 1996 show Israeli economic activity has stabilised, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
It said most indicators registered a slight increase in December over November or no change. However, the increase in domestic demand continued to slow as did industrial exports.

The bureau said retail sales by retail chains grew at an annual pace of 5.3 percent in November and December, marking a continuation of the near steady decline in growth since the start of the year. In the first quarter, retail sales were running at a 15.3-19.7 percent pace.
Industrial-export growth slowed in December to a 5.8 percent annual rate from 7.5 percent in November and more than 10 percent during most of the second half of 1996, the bureau said.
Imports of capital goods rose 1.2 percent on the month before in December following seven months of month-on-month declines, the bureau said.
Imports of production inputs also rose at a 1.2 percent rate in the month after 10 months of declines.
Industrial output rose at a 5.3 percent pace in November, the last month for which there are figures, after rising at a 4.3 percent rate in the previous two months.
